# **PWAS**

# 

# **1\. Introduction**

## **What is the Procedural Weapon Animation System?**

The **Procedural Weapon Animation System (PWAS)** is a fully customizable, Blueprint-driven animation framework designed to deliver high-quality first-person weapon motion **without relying on traditional animation assets**.  
 Every effect—**recoil, sway, stance changes, walking cycles, aim offsets, breathing, camera kick, and more**—is generated **procedurally in real time**, making the system incredibly flexible and fast to iterate on.

PWAS requires **no C++ knowledge**, **no external animation packs**, and integrates seamlessly into any Unreal Engine FPS project.  
Everything runs through clean, modular Blueprints and fully editable DataAssets.

The goal of PWAS is simple:

**Give developers AAA-feeling first-person weapon animation that is easy to tune, easy to extend, and requires almost no pre-made animations.**

**Have some bugs, feature requests, wanting updates. Or just want to be in the community. Join the Discord server\! https://discord.gg/QSy94Heens**

---

## **What’s Included?**

### **✔ Procedural Weapon Actor Component**

Handles all core behavior: sway, recoil, movement cycles, stance adjustments, ADS logic, aim offsets, camera reactions, and more.

### **✔ Preset-Based Animation System**

All procedural settings are stored in **DataAssets**, allowing instant switching of weapon behavior without touching Blueprint logic.

### **✔ In-Editor Preset Editor Widget**

Tune every animation value *live* while the game is running. Create new presets or overwrite existing ones with a single click.

### 

### **✔ Demo Weapon Models**

Simple meshes for Rifles, SMGs, Pistols, LMGs, Shotguns, and Snipers. Each includes an example preset and an idle pose for immediate testing.

### **✔ Weapon-Class Preset Library**

Ready-to-use starting presets:

* Rifle

* Pistol

* SMG

* LMG

* Shotgun

* Sniper

All can be modified or duplicated to create new weapon styles.

### **✔ 300+ Tunable Parameters**

Organized by category, enabling fine control over every procedural effect.

### **✔ Optimized, Modular, Multiplayer-Safe**

All procedural animation executes **client-side only**, ensuring zero gameplay interference.

PWAS is designed for developers who want responsive, high-quality first-person weapon motion without the overhead of traditional animation production.

Perfect for:

🎮 Indie developers pursuing AAA feel  
🎨 Artists & designers who prefer visual tools over animation rigs  
🧪 Prototypers who need rapid iteration

No animation background required.

## **What Can It Do?**

PWAS provides an extensive suite of real-time procedural effects, including:

* Fully procedural recoil (per weapon, per ADS mode, camera/weapon influence)

* Screen shake & camera kick (for recoil)

* Breathing animation cycles

* Mouse-driven look sway

* Directional movement sway

* Walking and running motion loops

* Crouch and stance offsets (including separate walk and run values for crouch)

* Procedural ADS offsets & smoothing

* Collision pushback (weapon push when near walls)

* Equip/holster transitions

* ADS overrides (individual per-weapon)

* Fully clamped & adjustable angle limits

Every effect is modifiable.

## **What Makes PWAS Special?**

Unlike most procedural weapon animation packs, PWAS is:

* **Truly animation-optional** (no skeleton animations required)

* **Fully exposed and editable visually**

* **Designed for large-scale production workflows**

* **Extremely configurable and expandable**

* **Built around a complete preset ecosystem**

* **Perfect for teams and solo developers alike**

This is not just a collection of effects—it is a **complete procedural animation framework** tailored for FPS weapon systems.

This was mainly built for first person projects. I haven’t tested using third person, but I genuinely see no reason as to why that wouldn’t work. As it does the exact same thing in first or third person. I would expect it to work just fine if you blend the procedural animations with the upper body correctly

# **2\. System Overview**

The Procedural Weapon Animation System is built around a **modular, data-driven architecture** that allows every weapon to behave uniquely while sharing the same underlying animation logic. Instead of hardcoding behavior inside Blueprints, PWAS separates logic, animation data, and runtime behavior into clean, interchangeable parts.

This section explains how these systems work together and what each component is responsible for.

---

## **2.1 High-Level Architecture**

PWAS is composed of four core elements:

1. **Procedural Weapon Component**

   * Handles all mathematical processing for sway, recoil, offsets, stance changes, etc.

   * Outputs clean, ready-to-apply transforms every frame.

2. **Weapon Preset DataAssets**

   * Store all animation-related parameters (recoil settings, sway intensity, ADS offsets, curves, etc.).

   * Allow instant switching between weapon behaviors without modifying logic.

3. **Animation Blueprint Integration**

   * Applies the weapon’s calculated transforms to the arms, weapon bone, and IK systems.

   * Handles Two-Bone IK, FABRIK, and pose blending.

4. **Editor-Level Preset Editor Widget**

   * Enables live tuning of procedural parameters.

   * Allows saving and reloading presets in real time.

Together, these parts create a flexible and scalable procedural animation pipeline.

---

## **2.2 How the System Works**

Every tick (can be changed via variables in the AC\_ProceduralWeaponAnimationSystem, added to the player blueprint. Default value is 0,01, changing this value will most likely change the procedural animations behaviour). PWAS performs a predictable, optimized sequence of operations:

### **1\. Gather Player Input & Weapon State**

* Mouse delta

* Movement direction & speed

* ADS state

* Crouch state

* Recoil request (from firing events)

* Weapon-specific modifiers

### **2\. Apply Sway, Breathing, and Motion Calculations**

The system accumulates all relevant offsets:

* View sway

* Movement sway

* Breathing noise

* Idle adjustments

* Running/Walking motion loops

* Stance modifiers

### **3\. Compute Recoil**

If the weapon is firing:

* Apply camera kick

* Add weapon rotation & translation impulses

* Use per-weapon recoil curves from the preset

### **4\. Apply ADS Overrides (If Aiming)**

* Blend to ADS offsets

* Modify sway intensity

* Adjust recoil scale

* Apply ADS smoothing curve

### **5\. Send Final Offsets to the Animation Blueprint**

The AnimBP receives:

* Weapon location offset

* Weapon rotation offset

* Left-hand IK target position

* Elbow pole vector

* Any additional transform modifiers

### **6\. IK Solvers Apply Hand Alignment**

The Animation Blueprint finalizes:

* Two-Bone IK or FABRIK for left-hand placement

* Right-hand attachment (usually bound to `hand_r`, but attaching to `ik_hand_gun` should be preferred)

* Pose blending

At this point, the frame is complete.

---

## **2.3 Core Components Explained**

### **Procedural Weapon Component**

This is the main logic driver. Its responsibilities include:

* Sway calculation

* Movement cycles (walk/run)

* ADS transitions

* Camera/weapon recoil

* Breathing simulation

* Crouch/stance adjustments

* Weapon collision pushing

* Runtime blending & smoothing

You can treat it as a “brain” generating all procedural motion.

---

### 

### 

### 

### **Weapon Preset DataAssets**

Every weapon in PWAS uses a preset that defines:

* Recoil strength, curve shape, randomness

* Sway intensity and smoothing

* ADS behavior

* Walking/Running cycle parameters

* Crouch offsets

* Look-based motion

* Clamping limits

* Collision pushback behavior

* Stance multipliers

* Weapon-class feel tuning

Presets allow two weapons of the same type (e.g., two rifles) to behave completely differently just by adjusting values.

---

### **Animation Blueprint Layer**

The AnimBP applies weapon offsets to the first-person arms rig using:

* Transform (Modify) Bone nodes

* Additive pose offsets

* FABRIK or Two-Bone IK

* IK pole vectors

* Blended state machines

It is only responsible for:

* Receiving offsets

* Applying them

* Solving the hand positions

All behavior logic is external and comes from the procedural component.

---

### **Preset Editor Widget**

A custom UI built for:

* Real-time tuning

* Browsing weapons

* Modifying all parameters

* Saving new presets

* Overwriting existing ones

It allows designers and artists to adjust weapon behavior:

* Without touching Blueprints

* Without restarting the editor

* Without recompiling anything

This significantly speeds up iteration. Something to be aware of when saving a preset, you cannot overwrite data assets that are being referenced. This is due to the engine.

## **2.6 Design Philosophy**

PWAS is built on three principles:

### **1\. Data-Driven**

The system relies on presets, not hardcoded logic, ensuring scalability.

### **2\. Fully Procedural**

Everything—from recoil to stance adjustments—is mathematical and generated at runtime.

### **3\. Artist-Friendly**

Live editing and visual tools allow quick tuning and minimal technical overhead.

# **3\. Installation & Setup**

This section explains how to install the Procedural Weapon Animation System, set up your project for first-time use, and verify that everything is working correctly. The setup process is intentionally streamlined so developers can begin testing procedural weapon motion within minutes.

---

## **3.1 Adding the System to Your Project**

### **1\. Add it from your library**

### **2\. Verify Activation**

If the folder **“Procedural Weapon Animation System”**  appears, it’s successfully installed to the project.

---

## 

## 

## 

## **3.2 Recommended Project Settings**

The weapon models will most likely start to clip into the camera. Opening the Project Settings, searching for **“Near Clip Plane”** and setting the value to something low, like 0,01 will fix this.

---

## **3.3 Adding the component**

### **1\. Open your character blueprint**

Add the component AC\_ProceduralWeaponAnimationSystem. Rename it to PWAS if you want to shorten the name.

**Add Component → Procedural Weapon Component**

This component will now:

* Calculate sway

* Apply recoil

* Handle ADS transitions

* Generate weapon offsets

* Provide Left-Hand IK positions

* Handle movement animation cycles

### **2\. Create MouseX and MouseY Variables**

Find your Look input and get the axis for the mouse x and plug the value into the newly created variable **MouseX**. Do the same for the **MouseY** variable, but for the look up/down. These are used for procedural look sway.

### **2\. Add tag to your character mesh**

For the system to find and select the correct mesh to get skeleton bones from, you need to add the tag **FPMesh** to your skeleton.

### **3\. Create or open your weapon master Blueprint**

Add a new variable, call it something like “WeaponPreset”. The variable type should be DA\_WeaponPreset

### **4\. Assign a Preset**

In the class details:  
 **Weapon Preset → Select a preset (e.g., DA\_WPP\_Rifle)**

The weapon now uses all procedural settings defined in the preset.

---

## **3.4 Skeleton & Socket Requirements**

### **Important Notes**

* The weapon mesh **must** attach to the character’s `ik_hand_gun / hand_r` or a socket attached to that bone.

* The left-hand IK socket should be placed *on the weapon mesh*, not the arms rig.

The transform bone is to set the actual base transform and should be used to create the actual finish pose. The elbow location is there to adjust the elbow, so it won’t warp or look bad.

# **Left Hand IK & Reload Animations (PWAS)**

**PWAS uses FABRIK-based Left Hand IK to keep the support hand correctly attached to the weapon, even when the weapon is moved procedurally (recoil, sway, offsets, etc.).**

**To prevent Left Hand IK from overriding reload animations, PWAS supports montage-driven IK control using animation curves.**

**This is only required for the “Sockets” workflow, as weapons made with ik\_hand\_gun bone in mind do not need this. If you have any of my weapon animation packs, you do not need to do this. As I did animate with the ik\_hand\_gun bone.**

---

## **How Left Hand IK Works in PWAS**

* **Left Hand IK is applied at the very end of the AnimGraph**

* **FABRIK is used for maximum robustness with procedural weapon motion**

* **The IK alpha is controlled by an animation curve during reloads**

* **Outside of reloads, Left Hand IK is fully enabled by default**

**This ensures:**

* **No snapping**

* **No hand drifting**

* **Reload animations remain fully authorable**

---

## **Required Reload Montage Setup**

### **1️⃣ Add a float curve to the reload montage**

**In your reload Anim Montage, add a Float Curve named:**

**![][image17]**

**The curves is under the “Notifies” tab**  
**![][image18]**

**Name it “ReloadAlpha” This name is very important, if it’s wrong it will not work.**

### **2️⃣ Author the curve values**

Use the curve to control how much **Left Hand IK** is applied during the reload.

Recommended behavior:

* `1.0` → Animation fully controls the left hand

* `0.0` → Left Hand IK fully enabled (hand glued to weapon)

### **Typical curve pattern:**

* Fade from **0 →1** when the hand leaves the weapon

* Stay at **1** while reloading

* Fade from **1 → 0** when the hand returns to the weapon

This gives smooth, natural reloads without fighting the IK.

![][image19]

**This is from the rifle reload example included in the pack. This shows you an example on how to utilize this.**

---

## **Anim Blueprint Setup (Already Included in PWAS)**

PWAS reads the curve automatically in the AnimBP:

* `Get Curve Value (ReloadAlpha)`

* The value is stored as `Reload Alpha`

* This value drives the **FABRIK Alpha** for Left Hand IK

![][image20]![][image21]

**This curve needs to be connected to a ReloadAlpha variable, this controls the alpha of the FABRIK node which is laying at the very end of the procedural animations in the AnimGraph.**

---

## **4 Setting Up A Weapon**

### **1\. Left Hand IK & Muzzle**

Open up your weapon model and add a socket for **Muzzle**. Adjust it so the location is at the end of the barrel. This will be a socket used for checking weapon collisions. Next add another socket called **LeftHandIK**, this will change the location and rotation for the left hand. This is something that needs to be manually adjusted. I recommend pressing play with the mode **selected viewport**, pressing **F8** to detach from the character, then getting close to the left hand and adjusting the socket. This will update live as you change it, either use another screen for changing the socket location and rotation, or simply adjust the window size so you will see both the viewport and the window for adjusting the socket.

**![][image22]**  
**![][image23]**

### **2\. Right Hand IK**

The right probably won’t be aligned correctly. Modifying the right hand is a bit different than the left hand IK as it does not require a socket. Instead it’s at the bottom under the page **Holster / Adjuster**, there are values called **Right Hand Adjuster Loc** & **Right Hand Adjuster Rot**. These will be the values adjusting the right hand. You can also press Open **F8** to detach and fly around the weapon for a closer look, just remember to press **TAB** first so the **Procedural Weapon Editor** window is open.

Instead of creating a new save for every change, you can also edit the **DataAssets** while the game is running, though it won’t update live. This can save time, especially for quick changes. Just remember to press stop, then play again to see the change.

### 

### **3\. Setting up your character**

There are events that need to be called  to the **AC\_PWAS**. I recommend looking inside the **BP\_FPCharacter** and copying what you see there when it comes to the **AC\_PWAS**.

**OnFired:** This is called when you fire.  
**StopFire:** This is called when you stop firing (optional and only used to reset **First Shot Kick**)  
**ToggleAim:** This is called when you start and stop aiming.

**InitPlayer:** This is called when the character is spawned/initiated. This is where you add the references to your player, camera and weapon mesh if you have one ready.  
**ToggleRun:** This is called when you start and stop running.  
**ToggleHolster:** This is called when you want to start and stop the holster position. In the example blueprint (**BP\_FPCharacter**) This is used when changing weapons, also using a change weapon delay, before actually spawning the new weapon and calling **ToggleHolster** with false check.  
**ToggleStance:** This is called when you start and stop crouching.  
**UpdateStats:** This is called when you need to update the procedural stats. Usually when you equip a new weapon and actually want to update your character's procedural values.  
**UpdateWeaponRef:** This is also usually called when equipping a new weapon, as you also need to update the weapon mesh ref. Static and Skeletal is accepted. This is just to get the sockets.  
**OpenProceduralUI:** This is used to open the actual **Procedural Weapon Editor**. This is where you will adjust the values live. This is not meant for gameplay and is for adjusting values before saving it and creating a new **DataAsset** with the selected values. Saving a preset can only be done within the editor, not a packaged game.

# 

# **5\. Weapon Presets**

Weapon Presets are the heart of the Procedural Weapon Animation System.  
 They define how a weapon *feels*, *moves*, *recoils*, *aims*, and *behaves* in every gameplay state.

Instead of editing Blueprint code or animation graphs, all procedural behavior is stored inside a **single DataAsset**, making it easy to swap, duplicate, and iterate on weapon profiles.

This section explains how presets work, how they are structured, and how to create or edit them.

Remember to duplicate from the correct premade preset, depending on your setup. For animations made with **ik\_hand\_gun** in mind, the ones like **DA\_WPP\_Rifle** should be used. For setups where you would attach the weapon/socket to the **hand\_r**, duplicate from **DA\_WPP\_Rifle\_Socket**. This has values set for **adjusted** settings and proper aim height. 

Weapons attached to the **ik\_hand\_gun** like you would do with **hand\_r** needs to have the i**k\_hand\_gun** bone forced to have 0 in transform and rotation to get the correct procedural values, this means that when aiming. The aiming Z value needs to be a lot lower to accommodate height, so something like \-160 in Z aiming value is not unusual.

## **5.1 What Is a Weapon Preset?**

A **Weapon Preset** is a reusable DataAsset that stores every procedural animation parameter for a weapon, including:

* Sway intensity & smoothing

* Recoil (strength, curves, randomness, recovery)

* ADS offsets & blend speeds

* Walking/Running/Breathing cycles

* Movement sway responsiveness

* Pose adjustments (idle, crouch, run)

* Camera kick behavior

* Clamps & angle limits

* Weapon-class feel modifiers

Each weapon actor references one preset. Changing the preset instantly changes how the weapon animates.

## 

## **5.2 Creating a New Preset**

### **Method 1: Duplicate an Existing Preset**

Recommended for most users.

1. Navigate to:  
    `Content/ProceduralWeaponAnimation/Data/DataAssets/Presets/`

2. Duplicate a preset (e.g., **DA\_WPP\_Rifle**) Then call it whatever you want (**WPP** stands for **Weapon Procedural Preset**). So you can call your custom presets **CPP**. A good practice is to never move, delete or modify the premade presets. Place your custom ones in  `Content/ProceduralWeaponAnimation/Data/Custom`

3. Assign it to your weapon actor

**Never touch or use DA\_WPP\_Temp. This is only used when changing live values using the Procedural Editor during runtime, this holds the temporary values.**

---

## 

## 

## **5.3 Editing a Preset (Live in Editor)**

Using the **Preset Editor Widget**:

1. On a key event, add **Open Procedural UI** from the **AC\_PWAS**. This opens up the actual editor. **TAB** is the default key if you are using the included character blueprint.

2. Load a preset you duplicated.

3. Adjust sliders, curves, rotations, and numeric values.

4. See changes in real time while the game is running. There are buttons at the top that will activate the procedural animations, like **Start Walk**. This will start the procedural animations for the walking, you can then adjust the values without having to walk manually to see the results. **Do not change weapons while editing, as this will load the new values from that weapon into the Weapon Editor. Only if you call “Update Stats” of course**.  
     
5. Save the preset using a custom name. Something like **DA\_CPP\_** is a good prefix. **Do keep in mind that you can not overwrite presets that are being referenced**.

This allows rapid weapon feel iteration without leaving PIE mode.

![][image24]

**These values within “Recoil Stats” will change the recoil animation feeling a lot. “Recoil Fire” controls the interp values while firing, “Recoil Reset” values will activate when you stop firing.**

---

## **5.4 Best Practices for Preset Design**

### **✔ Use presets per weapon class, then refine per weapon**

E.g., all rifles start from RiflePreset → then adjust per model.

### **✔ Duplicate presets before extreme experimentation**

Keeps a stable baseline.

## 

## 

## 

## **5.5 Extra Info**

Some values may not seem to change a lot, especially the recoil. A lot of the time, changing the stiffness and velocity will do a LOT. So if you are changing some values and it doesn’t seem to do anything, try to play a little with the stiffness and velocity.

**6\. Procedural Weapon Editor**

![][image25]

This is where **PWAS** will help you drastically. Let's start with the main stuff from the top. You can load and save presets. The **Enable Preview** bar has different buttons based on the page you are on. **Recoil, Camera, Idle** will have the same preview bar. **Walk, Run, Crouch**. Will have the same, **Collision** will not have one. Then lastly the **Holster / Adjuster** Will have its own. The buttons for **Recoil, Camera, Idle**, etc are different pages. You should go through this menu to learn what is where. In the end it’s pretty self explanatory. You can toggle the check marks to disable or enable stuff under the designated values. The image above shows some of the **Recoil Stats**. Right under you can enable or disable **Weapon Recoil**. This will skip recoil code when firing. You can either drag the sliders, click the numbers on the right to change it to a specific number, or you can also click and drag the numbers for a more controllable value change.

**Keep in mind**. When modifying the **adjuster** values, you will have to modify the procedural aiming values again. So to not get frustrated, please adjust the **adjuster** first before moving on to the aiming.

**Some information about the sliders. Most of the movement itself will come from the “Spring” which is used for almost every procedural animation to make it more realistic.**

**Multiplier**: Is multiplying the values, so 2 will double the values.

**Stiffness:** How hard the spring will be

**Damping:** How much the spring will lose energy (Can lower the amount of bouncing)

**Mass:** How heavy the feeling is

**Velocity:** The velocity of the spring (Usually not something you need to touch, is mostly used for hard kicks like recoil. Lowering this a tiny will also help eliminate the bouncing)

**These are values inside the spring, these are really important as it changes the feeling and reaction of the procedural animations. The rest of the values which are not “Spring”, are usually just for the amount.**

**These are values you will have to play around and learn, as everything it’s pretty self explanatory. Learning this is really easy.**

**![][image26]**

When adjusting for aim location and rotation, I would highly suggest that you enable **Align Crosshair**. This shows a big thin cross which will help you see the middle of the screen.The scale of the crosshair will help you align the weapon properly.

# **7\. Troubleshooting**

Even with correct setup, procedural animation systems can behave unpredictably due to IK complexity, incorrect socket placement, conflicting animation layers, or improper AnimGraph ordering.  
This section lists the most common issues that may be encountered while using PWAS, along with their likely causes and solutions.

---

# 

# **7.1 Left Hand IK Problems**

---

## **Issue: Left Hand Drifts Away From the Grip**

**Cause:**

* Weapon procedural offsets are applied *after* IK in the AnimGraph.

* Incorrect Effector Space settings.

* Missing ADS override.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Move FABRIK / Two-Bone IK to the **bottom** of the AnimGraph.  
 ✔ Ensure Effector Transform Space \= **Bone Space / Parent Bone Space**  
 ✔ Update LeftHandIK\_Position every frame in the Event Graph.

---

## **Issue: Elbow Flips or Rotates Unnaturally**

**Cause:**

* Pole vector not applied or incorrect.

* ElbowDirection not passed in world space.

* No LeftHandElbow socket on weapon.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Change the value of the **Elbow Target** until it looks correct.

---

## 

## 

## **Issue: Left Hand Rotates Wrong or Is Upside Down**

**Cause:**

* Incorrect orientation of LeftHandIK socket.

* Gun mesh’s forward axis differs from expected orientation.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Rotate the LeftHandIK socket.  
 ✔ Adjust socket orientation in Persona and test in PIE.

---

## **Issue: Hand Pops or Snaps During ADS**

**Cause:**

* ADS offset too large.

* IK smoothing too low.

* Running → ADS transition too abrupt.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Reduce ADS translation offset.  
 ✔ Increase ADS blend time.  
 ✔ Use weapon-class presets as baseline (rifles, pistols, SMGs).

---

# 

# 

# 

# **7.2 Weapon Alignment Issues**

---

## **Issue: Weapon Doesn’t Line Up With Camera in ADS**

**Cause:**

* Incorrect ADS offsets in preset.

* Wrong bone used in Modify Transform node.

* Camera FOV mismatch.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Use **small, incremental adjustments** to ADS offsets.  
 ✔ Ensure the **ik\_hand\_gun bone** is being modified—not the hand bone.  
 ✔ Verify camera FOV matches your design.  
 ✔ Adjust aim transform and rotation.

---

## **Issue: Weapon Clips Into Camera When Firing**

**Cause:**

* Kickback value too high.

* Recoil curve overshoots.

* Movement sway stacking with recoil.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Reduce Kickback distance.  
 ✔ Clamp recoil curve.  
 ✔ Lower ADS sway multiplier.  
 ✔ Lower value of **Near Clip Plane** in the **Project Settings**

---

## **Issue: Weapon Floats Away From Hands During Movement**

**Cause:**

* Weapon transform applied before locomotion blending.

* Incorrect ordering in AnimGraph.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Apply procedural weapon transform **after state machine / locomotion**.  
 ✔ IK nodes must be at the very **end**.

---

# **7.3 Recoil Issues**

---

## **Issue: Recoil Is Too Strong or Uncontrollable**

**Cause:**

* Pitch/Yaw values too high.

* No ADS reduction.

* Incorrect curve scaling.


**Fix:**  
 ✔ Start with small values: e.g., Pitch \= 1.5, Yaw \= 0.2.  
 ✔ Ensure ADS multipliers reduce recoil by at least 50–80%.  
 ✔ Check that your curve is normalized (0–1 range).  
 ✔ Enable recoil return and adjust values.

---

## 

## 

## **Issue: Recoil Looks Delayed or Laggy**

**Cause:**

* Too much smoothing.

* Recovery speed is too low.

* Update Animation graph not pulling values every frame.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Lower smoothing values.  
 ✔ Increase RecoilRecoverySpeed.  
 ✔ Ensure “Blueprint Update Animation” event is executing.

---

## **Issue: Camera and Weapon Recoil Don't Match**

**Cause:**

* Camera recoil multipliers too strong or weak.

* Weapon recoil applied at different curve timing.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Match camera kick to weapon pitch strength.  
 ✔ Use the same recoil curve for both (if desired).

---

# 

# 

# 

# **7.4 Sway & Movement Issues**

---

## **Issue: Weapon Feels Too Floaty**

**Cause:**

* Sway smoothing too high.

* Mouse-based sway too strong.

* Movement sway amplitude too large.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Lower LookSwaySmoothness.  
 ✔ Reduce sway amplitude.  
 ✔ Increase Return Interp speed.

---

## **Issue: Weapon Shakes or Vibrates**

**Cause:**

* Noise sway amplitude too high.

* FPS too low for current smoothing.

* Effector updates not being applied consistently.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Reduce NoiseAmplitude.  
 ✔ Increase NoiseSmoothing.  
 ✔ Ensure values pull every frame.

---

## 

## **Issue: Running Sway Looks Unrealistic**

**Cause:**

* Cycle amplitude too extreme.

* Run-lowered pose not set.

* Movement influence is too high.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Reduce run sway amplitude.  
 ✔ Add a run-lowered offset.  
 ✔ Reduce direction sway influence.

---

# **7.5 ADS & Transition Problems**

---

## **Issue: ADS Feels Jittery**

**Cause:**

* Conflicting animation layers.

* Too much smoothing or low framerate.

* Sway conflicting with ADS offsets.  
* ADS from premade preset not matching

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Ensure ADS uses a **Layered Blend Per Bone**.  
 ✔ Increase ADS blend time slightly.  
 ✔ Reduce ADS sway values.

✔ Duplicate from the correct premade preset. Presets ending in Socket will be more correct if you use the old (hand\_r) method. In the end, values needed are fully depending on socket and adjusted location/rotation.

---

## 

## **Issue: ADS Snaps Abruptly**

**Cause:**

* Blend time too short.

* ADS curve too harsh.

* Large ADS offsets.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Increase ADS blend time (0.15–0.25 sec recommended).  
 ✔ Use a soft ADS curve (ease-in / ease-out).  
 ✔ Lower ADS translation offset magnitude.

---

# **7.6 Animation Blueprint & Graph Errors**

---

## **Issue: Weapon Not Updating at All**

**Cause:**

* Missing references in Event Graph.

* Procedural Weapon Component not assigned.

* Variables not bound to Modify Transform nodes.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Print debug values inside Update Animation.  
 ✔ Reassign weapon component reference.  
 ✔ Verify AnimBP variables are hooked up.

---

## 

## **Issue: IK Nodes Cause Broken Arm Poses**

**Cause:**

* Effector space incorrect.

* Wrong chain bones selected.

* ADS or run pose interfering.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Use **Bone Space** for IK targets.  
 ✔ Confirm correct upperarm\_l → hand\_l chain.  
 ✔ Apply IK AFTER all blending.

---

# **7.7 Socket & Mesh Issues**

---

## **Issue: Weapon Seems Rotated Wrong in Hand**

**Cause:**

* Gun mesh orientation differs from standard FPS conventions.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Reorient mesh or adjust weapon socket rotation.

---

## **Issue: Left Hand Never Reaches IK Target**

**Cause:**

* IK target too far away.

* Arm length limitation.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Adjust LeftHandIK socket closer to hand.  
 ✔ Reduce exaggerated recoil or movement offsets.

---

# **7.8 Editor / Live Preset Editing Issues**

---

## **Issue: Preset Changes Don’t Apply During PIE**

**Cause:**

* Wrong preset selected.

* Weapon uses runtime-loaded instance.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Select the correct preset in the editor window.  
 ✔ Ensure the weapon actor loads the assigned preset on BeginPlay.

---

## **Issue: Overwriting a Preset Doesn’t Save Changes**

**Cause:**

* Read-only preset in packaged builds.

* Missing editor permissions.

**Fix:**  
 ✔ Preset saving only works inside the **Editor**.  
 ✔ Use Create New Preset instead of Save if overwriting fails.

---

# 

# **7.9 General Debug Tips**

### **✔ Print all offsets (recoil, sway, ADS) every frame**

If one value isn’t updating, you’ve found the problem.

### **✔ Check AnimGraph node order**

Most issues come from IK or procedural transforms being applied in the wrong place.

### **✔ Toggle animation layers on/off**

This helps find conflicting blends.

### **✔ Test with default weapon meshes**

If IK works on defaults but not on your mesh, the issue is socket placement.

### **✔ Reset preset to default values**

If everything is broken, start from a clean baseline.

---

# 

# 

# **7.10 Summary**

Most issues stem from:

* Incorrect socket placement

* Wrong IK ordering

* Effector/JT space misconfiguration

* ADS blending conflicting with sway

* Excessively large preset values

Once these areas are validated, PWAS becomes remarkably stable, predictable, and easy to work with.

**One thing to be aware of is: GM\_Base has the character blueprint BP\_FPCharacter. This is the character with poses/animations made with ik\_hand\_gun bone in mind.**

**GM\_Socket used the character blueprint BP\_FPCharacter\_Socket. Which uses the ABP\_Socket, weapons and weapon presets with the suffix \_Socket. If you usually attach the weapon to the hand\_r bone. Follow the example animation blueprint of the ABP\_Socket. Also duplicate presets from the \_Socket to get a more correct premade preset.**

# **Final Summary**

Thank you for using the **Procedural Weapon Animation System**.  
This system was designed to give developers a flexible, animation-free foundation for creating responsive, immersive first-person weapon behavior with minimal setup and maximum creative control.

With PWAS, you now have:

* A fully procedural animation pipeline

* A powerful preset-driven workflow

* Dynamic recoil, sway, ADS, and movement systems

* A robust Left-Hand IK solution

* Clean integration with your Animation Blueprint

* Tools that scale effortlessly across dozens of weapons

Whether you're building a prototype or a full production FPS title, PWAS aims to simplify development, enhance visual fidelity, and empower both technical and non-technical team members to fine-tune weapon feel directly inside Unreal Engine.

Thank you again for choosing PWAS — and best of luck with your project.
